alternatives.root_cause: A feature flag affecting the cart code path was flipped in flagd, pushing cart into a slow or failing branch.
alternatives.why_not: The canonical cart flag produces errors rather than pure latency, and flagd serves ad, recommendation and product-reviews too — none of those alerted, so a flagd-side change is less likely to be confined to cart.

alternatives.root_cause: cart exhausted a local resource (connection pool, threads or memory) and queued requests behind it.
alternatives.why_not: Plausible and indistinguishable from the outside, but exhaustion usually escalates into errors and restarts rather than a steady one-minute-ahead latency warning; I would demote it until cart's saturation metrics say otherwise.

verdict.summary: The cart service became slow — its backing store (valkey-cart, not in the graph) started responding slowly, so cart requests piled up waiting and the latency propagated upstream to checkout, frontend, frontend-proxy and the load-generator.
verdict.reasoning: cart alerted a full minute before everything else, and every other alerting service is a transitive caller of cart (frontend -> cart, checkout -> cart, frontend-proxy -> frontend, load-generator drives the front door). Nothing downstream-only of cart's peers (product-catalog, currency, shipping, payment) alerted on its own, which argues the fault is at cart rather than something cart and others share. The symptom set is latency warnings with no error alerts, which fits waiting rather than failing: cart is a thin service whose time is dominated by its key-value store, so a slow valkey-cart is the most natural mechanism. valkey-cart being explicitly absent from the dependency graph means a store-side fault would surface exactly this way — as unexplained latency at cart with no alerting child.
open_questions: cart's own latency breakdown: time in handler vs time in redis/valkey client calls
valkey-cart health: memory usage, eviction, RDB/AOF fsync pauses, slowlog
cart container CPU throttling, GC pauses and thread/connection pool saturation
flagd evaluation latency and whether any flag affecting the cart path changed around 00:45
whether cart returned errors or just slow 200s, and whether deadlines were hit upstream
